# Apply Progress: Persistent Navigation Shell

Mode: Strict TDD. Artifact store: hybrid (engram + openspec).

## Slice 1 (PR1: Shell + Nav Items) — 11/11 complete

Branch: `persistent-navigation-01-shell-nav` (from tracker `persistent-navigation`, from `develop`). Verified PASS (Engram `sdd/persistent-navigation/verify-report`).

- [x] 1.1-1.11 — see prior revision detail (unchanged). Commits: `6afe582`, `cdec0b5`, `fe155ee`.

## Slice 2 (PR2: Group-List State + Switcher + D4 Persistence) — 14/14 complete

Branch: `persistent-navigation-02-group-state-switcher` (from tip of Slice 1 branch). Targets Slice 1 branch as PR2 (feature-branch-chain).

- [x] 2.1-2.14 — see prior revision detail (unchanged). Commits: `daddd02`, `0ef2ca4`, `4e9190c`.

Review budget: Slice 1 tip → Slice 2 tip = 769 changed lines (forecast ~350-420).

## Slice 3 (PR3: Mobile Add Expense FAB) — 8/8 complete

Branch: `persistent-navigation-03-fab` (from tip of Slice 2 branch `persistent-navigation-02-group-state-switcher`). Feature-branch-chain: targets Slice 2 branch as PR3.

- [x] 3.1 RED — extended `frontend/tests/pages/dashboard.test.tsx`: added a `useIsMobile` module mock (default `false`, per-test override) and a "mobile Add Expense FAB" describe block: mobile hides the header button (asserted via `within(header).queryByRole(...)` to avoid a trivially-passing count-only assertion), shows exactly one "Add Expense" control (the FAB), and clicking it opens Dashboard's existing `ExpenseForm` (proven via its description placeholder). Desktop test asserts the header button is present and no second "Add Expense" control exists.
- [x] 3.2 RED — extended `frontend/tests/pages/expenses-page.test.tsx`: added `ExpensesPage` import + mocks for `AuthContext`, `ActiveGroupContext`, and `shared/api/dashboardHooks` (previously this file only tested `ExpenseForm` directly — same repo-pre-existing filename/content mismatch noted, not fixed here as it's out of this slice's scope). New "ExpensesPage — mobile Add Expense FAB" describe block mirrors 3.1 (mobile hides header, FAB opens existing dialog; desktop unaffected) plus a third case asserting `disabled={!summary}` carries over to the FAB while the dashboard summary is still loading.
- [x] 3.3 RED — new `frontend/tests/shared/ui/AddExpenseFab.test.tsx`: behavioral a11y spec (default + custom `aria-label`, Plus icon present, fires `onClick`, renders no `dialog` role, `disabled` blocks clicks) plus a static "route guard" describe block that reads the source of `TransfersPage.tsx`/`SavingsPage.tsx`/`GroupsPage.tsx`/`ProfilePage.tsx` via `node:fs` and asserts none of them contain the string `AddExpenseFab` — satisfies spec scenario "Other pages never show the FAB" without needing to stand up each page's full dependency graph.
- [x] 3.4 GREEN — created `frontend/src/shared/ui/AddExpenseFab.tsx`: presentational-only per design A6 (`onClick`, `disabled?`, `label?` props; no `useIsMobile()`, no dialog state, no fetching). Fixed bottom-right, positioned above the mobile tab bar (`bottom-[calc(4.5rem+env(safe-area-inset-bottom))]`), `aria-label={label ?? "Add Expense"}`, Plus icon, `expense`-red styling matching the existing "Add Expense" button color convention.
- [x] 3.5 GREEN — exported `AddExpenseFab` from `frontend/src/shared/ui/index.tsx`.
- [x] 3.6 GREEN — modified `frontend/src/pages/dashboard/ui/DashboardPage.tsx`: added `useIsMobile()`, wrapped the header "Add Expense" `Button` in `{!isMobile && ...}`, rendered `{isMobile && <AddExpenseFab onClick={() => setCreateExpenseOpen(true)} />}` as a sibling right after the header.
- [x] 3.7 GREEN — modified `frontend/src/pages/expenses/ui/ExpensesPage.tsx`: `isMobile` already existed (used for row-tap vs row-menu mode); wrapped the header "Add Expense" `Button` in `{!isMobile && ...}`, rendered `<AddExpenseFab disabled={!summary} onClick={() => setExpenseDialog({ mode: "form", expense: null })} />` on mobile. The empty-state "Add your first expense" CTA inside the list body was left untouched (out of scope per task). Confirmed 3.1-3.3 pass; also fixed 2 pre-existing TS errors surfaced by the new test mocks (missing `userId`/`budgeted` on the mock member, missing `isInitialLoading` on the mock `useDashboardSummary` return — both fields exist on the real hook/type and were just omitted in the new test fixtures).
- [x] 3.8 REFACTOR — grepped `frontend/src` for `AddExpenseFab`: only appears in `AddExpenseFab.tsx` (definition), `shared/ui/index.tsx` (export), `DashboardPage.tsx`, and `ExpensesPage.tsx` — no orphan usage, no leftover unused imports.

### Design Interpretation Notes (not deviations)

- "Fixed position" from task 3.3 is NOT asserted via a CSS class/computed-style check: this repo's vitest config has no `css: true`, so jsdom never applies the compiled Tailwind stylesheet, and the project's Strict TDD assertion-quality rules explicitly ban CSS-class assertions as brittle/non-behavioral. Instead, 3.3's spec covers everything actually observable and meaningful in RTL: accessible name/label, icon presence, click firing, disabled-blocks-click, and no owned dialog markup. The literal "position: fixed, above the tab bar" placement is implemented in the component per design (`fixed ... bottom-[calc(4.5rem+env(safe-area-inset-bottom))]`) and reviewable by inspection; it was not independently unit-tested.
- The "Other pages never show the FAB" scenario (3.3) is covered by a static source-guard test (asserts the 4 other pages never import `AddExpenseFab`) rather than fully rendering each page with its own dependency graph — cheaper, still a real assertion against production source (fails the moment someone adds the import), and avoids stacking 4 more heavyweight page-render mock setups for a negative-only assertion.
- `tests/pages/expenses-page.test.tsx` continues to have a filename/content mismatch (it originally only tested `ExpenseForm`, not `ExpensesPage`) — this slice's tasks.md explicitly named this file as the extension target, so the new `ExpensesPage` describe block was added alongside the existing `ExpenseForm` tests rather than renaming/splitting the file. Flagging for awareness, not fixed (out of scope).
- Two pre-existing TS type gaps in the new mock fixtures (`Member` needs `userId`/`budgeted`; `useDashboardSummary`'s return needs `isInitialLoading`) were fixed during GREEN/REFACTOR to keep `tsc --noEmit` clean — not a design deviation, just matching the real hook/type shapes.

## TDD Cycle Evidence (Slice 3)

observations.title: sdd/tanstack-query-migration/explore
observations.content:
## Exploration: Migrate frontend data-fetching to TanStack Query

### Current State (verified via codegraph + direct reads)

- React 19.2.6, react-dom 19.2.6, TS 6.0.3, Vite 8, vitest 4.1.6. No `@tanstack/*`, SWR, or any query-cache lib in `frontend/package.json` (confirmed) or anywhere in the repo (grepped "tanstack|QueryClient|swr|SWRConfig" repo-wide — zero hits). No existing QueryClient/Provider setup. React 19 is fully compatible with TanStack Query v5.
- Monorepo uses npm workspaces (`frontend`, `api`, `shared`), root `package-lock.json` committed, `packageManager: npm@10.8.2`. No unusual dependency-add ceremony found — adding a frontend dep is a normal `npm install <pkg> -w frontend` + commit the updated root lockfile. No CONTRIBUTING doc found describing a different process.
- `frontend/src/shared/api/client.ts` — `apiClient.fetch()`: fetch wrapper with 100ms in-flight de-dup Map (`pendingRequests`), Supabase session token injection, AbortSignal race. No real cache — same request 101ms later hits the network again. `client.test.ts` only asserts Authorization-header behavior (present/absent), NOT the dedup Map — safe to keep `apiClient.fetch` as the queryFn/mutationFn transport under a TanStack Query layer without breaking this test.
- `frontend/src/shared/api/useApiQuery.ts` — generic hook: `useState`/`useEffect`/`AbortController`, `refresh()` via counter, `isInitialLoading` derived from `settledGroupId !== groupId`. **No covering tests at all** (confirmed by codegraph blast-radius: "⚠️ no covering tests found"). 9 callers total: `dashboardHooks.ts` (4 hooks), `savingsHooks.ts` (1 hook), `GroupListContext.tsx` (1).
- `frontend/src/shared/api/dashboardHooks.ts` — `useDashboardSummary`, `useCategoriesList`, `useExpensesList`, `useTransfersList`, all thin `useApiQuery` wrappers with `apiClient.fetch` as fetcher. No dedicated test file.
- `frontend/src/shared/api/savingsHooks.ts` — `useSavingsGoals`, thin wrapper. No dedicated test file.
- `frontend/src/app/providers/GroupListContext.tsx` — `GroupListProvider`/`useGroupList()`, wraps `useApiQuery` keyed on `user?.id`, returns `{groups, loading, error, refresh}`. **No covering tests found** (per codegraph). Consumed by `GroupsPage.tsx` and `ActiveGroupSync.tsx`.
- `frontend/src/app/providers/ActiveGroupSync.tsx` — validates persisted active group id against `useGroupList()`'s fetched list; clears it if stale. Has its own test (`ActiveGroupSync.test.tsx`) that **mocks the entire `GroupListContext` module** (`vi.mock("./GroupListContext", ...)`), asserting only on `groups`/`loading`/`error` shape it supplies itself — decoupled from the real hook's internals, so this test survives the migration UNCHANGED as long as `useGroupList()`'s consumer-facing shape (`groups`, `loading`, `error`, `refresh`) is preserved (even if it's now a thin wrapper over `useQuery`).
- `frontend/src/app/providers/ActiveGroupContext.tsx` — separate "which group is active" concern (localStorage-persisted), untouched by this migration.
- `frontend/src/app/App.tsx` — provider tree: `BrowserRouter > AuthProvider > ActiveGroupProvider > Routes`; `GroupListProvider` + `ActiveGroupSync` are mounted only inside the protected `/*` route element, above `AppShell`. A `QueryClientProvider` would most naturally sit at/above `AuthProvider` (persists across login state) or just inside it — open question for proposal phase (also: should the QueryClient be cleared/reset on logout?).

### Consumers beyond the ones already named (new findings)

- **`frontend/src/pages/profile/ui/useProfileForm.ts`** — bypasses `apiClient` entirely: raw `fetch("/api/users/me")` / `fetch("/api/users", {method:"POST"})` with manual Authorization header construction, own `useState`/`useEffect` loading pattern. No AbortController, no dedup. Genuinely ad-hoc, not wired through `apiClient` or `useApiQuery` at all.
- **`frontend/src/widgets/dashboard/ui/BudgetCategories.tsx`** — calls `apiClient.fetch` **directly** (bypassing any entity API module) for three mutations: `category-create`, `category-update`, `transfer-create` (lines ~320, ~354, ~387), each followed by `onRefresh()` prop call. Also renders the category-delete trigger, but deletion itself is handled by the parent (`DashboardPage.handleDeleteCategory`).
- **`frontend/src/pages/dashboard/ui/DashboardPage.tsx`** — also calls `apiClient.fetch` directly (`category-delete`, line 152) instead of via an entity module, then calls both `refreshCategories()` and `refreshSummary()`.
- **`frontend/src/entities/member/useIncomeSession.ts`** — reducer-based session hook; `saveSession()` calls `groupApi.updateMemberIncome(memberId, amount)` for each changed member via `Promise.all`. Does NOT call any refresh itself — the consuming widget (IncomeOverview, per `DashboardPage`'s `onRefresh={handleRefresh}` prop) is responsible for refreshing `summary`/`categories` after a successful save. Has its own test `useIncomeSession.test.ts` (not yet read in full — verify field-name assumptions before implementation).
- Confirmed dead/unwired API surface: `groupApi.invitations.*`, `groupApi.archive.*`, `groupApi.transferOwnership` (all defined in `frontend/src/entities/group/index.ts`) have **zero consumers** anywhere in `frontend/src` — grepped repo-wide, only match is the definition file itself. Not in scope for invalidation-surface mapping since nothing currently calls them from the UI.

### Full mutation call-site → refresh map (confirms/extends the session's list)

| Mutation call site | Entity API used | What it refreshes afterward |
|---|---|---|
| `SavingsGoalForm.tsx` (`create`/`update`) | `savingsGoalApi` | `onSuccess` → `SavingsPage.refresh()` (the single `useSavingsGoals` query) |
| `SavingsGoalList.tsx` `handleDelete` | `savingsGoalApi.delete` | `onRefresh?.()` prop → same `refresh()` |
| `InlineAllocationEditor` (via `useContributionSession`) | `savingsGoalApi.upsertContribution`/`deleteContribution` | not directly checked here — flows through the same savings goal list refresh path; verify in propose phase |
| `DashboardPage.handleDeleteCategory` | raw `apiClient.fetch` (category-delete) | `refreshCategories()` + `refreshSummary()` |
| `BudgetCategories` add/edit/transfer handlers | raw `apiClient.fetch` | `onRefresh()` prop → `DashboardPage.handleRefresh` → both `refreshCategories()` + `refreshSummary()` |
| `ExpenseForm` (create/update) | `expenseApi` | `onSuccess` → caller's `refreshExpenses()`/`refreshSummary()` (or `handleRefresh()` on Dashboard) |
| `ExpensesPage.handleDeleteExpense`/`handleDeleteAllExpenses` | `expenseApi.delete`/`deleteAll` | `refreshExpenses()` + `refreshSummary()` |
| `TransfersPage.handleDeleteTransfer`/`handleDeleteAllTransfers` | `transferApi.delete`/`deleteAll` | `refreshTransfers()` + `refreshSummary()` |
| `useIncomeSession.saveSession` | `groupApi.updateMemberIncome` | none internally; consumer's `onRefresh` (Dashboard's `handleRefresh`) |
| `CreateGroupForm.tsx` | `groupApi.create` | `GroupsPage`'s `onCreated` → `useGroupList().refresh()` |
| `useProfileForm.submit` | raw `fetch` (not `apiClient`) | none — local state only, no shared query to invalidate |

Pattern: every list page independently threads 1-2 `refresh` closures by hand into every mutating child; there is no shared invalidation key space. A TanStack Query migration's invalidation surface is essentially: per-group `summary`, `categories`, `expenses` (paginated/filtered), `transfers` (paginated/filtered), `savingsGoals`, plus the cross-page `groups` list and `member income` (nested inside `summary.members`).

### Test coverage gaps and shape-breakage risk

- `useApiQuery.ts`, `dashboardHooks.ts`, `savingsHooks.ts`, `GroupListContext.tsx` — **zero dedicated unit tests** (confirmed via codegraph blast-radius AND `Glob` for `**/*.test.ts*`, no matches for any of these four).
- Page components (`DashboardPage.tsx`, `ExpensesPage.tsx`, `TransfersPage.tsx`, `SavingsPage.tsx`, `GroupsPage.tsx`) — no dedicated `.test.tsx` files either (confirmed via glob of all frontend test files — none match these page paths).
- The only test that touches the current hook *shape* indirectly is `ActiveGroupSync.test.tsx`, and it does so via a full module mock (`vi.mock("./GroupListContext")`), not the real `useApiQuery`/`GroupListContext` implementation — so it does NOT lock in field names like `loading`/`refresh` at the type level, only at the mock's own literal object. It WILL need updating only if `useGroupList()`'s returned property names change (e.g., `loading`→`isPending`), because the mock has to match whatever shape `ActiveGroupSync.tsx`'s implementation destructures.
- Widget/feature-level tests (`BudgetCategories.test.tsx`, `SavingsGoalList.test.tsx`, `SavingsGoalForm.test.tsx`, `InlineAllocationEditor.test.tsx`, `ExpenseForm.test.tsx`) mock the **entity API modules** directly (`savingsGoalApi`, `expenseApi`, `transferApi` via `vi.fn()`) and assert mutation calls + `onRefresh` prop invocation. These are decoupled from the caching layer and should survive the migration unchanged AS LONG AS entity API modules stay plain async functions (used as `queryFn`/`mutationFn`) and components keep accepting an `onRefresh`/`onSuccess`-style callback prop rather than reaching into `useQueryClient()` directly inside the presentational component.
- `client.test.ts` only asserts Authorization-header injection — safe regardless of caching-layer change, since `apiClient.fetch` can remain the low-level transport.
- Net risk: the four untested files most central to this migration (`useApiQuery`, `dashboardHooks`, `savingsHooks`, `GroupListContext`) are also the four with the LEAST existing safety net — new tests should be written as part of (not after) the migration, per the session brief's ask.

### Dependency-add precedent

- npm workspaces monorepo (root `package.json` `workspaces: ["frontend","api","shared"]`, `packageManager: npm@10.8.2`, root `package-lock.json` committed alongside `api/package-lock.json`). No separate per-package lockfiles beyond `api/package-lock.json`; frontend deps resolve through the root lockfile. No CONTRIBUTING/ADR found dictating a special process for adding a new frontend dependency — standard `npm install @tanstack/react-query -w frontend` + commit updated root lockfile is the established pattern (matches how e.g. `@base-ui/react`, `react-router-dom` etc. were presumably added — no anomalies in package.json).

### Open questions for sdd-propose

1. **`GroupListContext` fate**: keep as a thin Context wrapper around `useQuery` (preserves `ActiveGroupSync.test.tsx`'s mock shape and the `useGroupList()` call-site API across `GroupsPage.tsx`/`ActiveGroupSync.tsx` with a possibly smaller diff), or drop it and have `GroupsPage`/`ActiveGroupSync` call `useQuery` directly (removes an indirection layer but touches both consumers and requires updating `ActiveGroupSync.test.tsx`'s mock target). Affects blast radius directly.
2. **staleTime / refetchOnWindowFocus defaults**: session brief already frames this as "shared multi-user group-expense app — other members' edits should surface reasonably promptly" — needs a concrete default (e.g. `staleTime: 30s` + `refetchOnWindowFocus: true`) decided in propose, plus whether per-query overrides are needed (e.g. paginated expenses/transfers lists vs. summary).
3. **Returned-shape migration**: current consumers destructure `{data, loading, error, refresh, isInitialLoading}`; TanStack Query returns `{data, isPending, isFetching, isError, error, refetch}`. Decide: (a) expose TanStack's native shape everywhere and update every consumer + the (few) existing mocks/tests that reference `loading`/`refresh`, or (b) keep the thin-wrapper hooks (`useDashboardSummary`, etc.) returning today's shape internally backed by `useQuery`, minimizing consumer-side diff at the cost of one more indirection layer per hook. This is the single biggest design fork and should be resolved explicitly in the proposal.
4. **Mutation invalidation strategy**: replace hand-threaded `refresh()`/`onRefresh()` props with `useMutation({ onSuccess: () => queryClient.invalidateQueries(...) })`, but decide the query-key granularity (per-group vs. per-group-per-resource vs. per-group-per-resource-per-filter for paginated expenses/transfers) since over-broad invalidation could trigger unnecessary refetches and under-broad invalidation could miss the `summary`+`categories` cross-invalidation pattern seen in almost every current mutation handler.
5. **Direct `apiClient.fetch` call sites** (`BudgetCategories.tsx`, `DashboardPage.tsx` category-delete) and the fully ad-hoc `useProfileForm.ts` raw-`fetch` pattern: decide whether this migration also normalizes them into entity API modules + `useMutation`, or explicitly defers that cleanup to a follow-up change (scope-control decision).
6. **Supabase Realtime**: explicitly out of scope unless the proposal says otherwise — confirm no existing realtime subscription code exists (not found in this exploration) before deferring.
7. Dead/unused mutation surface (`groupApi.invitations`, `groupApi.archive`, `groupApi.transferOwnership`) — confirm these should be excluded from the migration's invalidation-surface work since they have no current UI consumers, or note if they're planned to be wired up in a near-future change (which would change the query-key design now to anticipate them).

### Artifacts / persistence note

OpenSpec write was NOT performed in this pass — this exploration executor was not given filesystem write access this session (no Write/Edit tool available) and top-level instructions explicitly restrict it to investigation only. observations.title: sdd/tanstack-query-migration/proposal
observations.content:
# Proposal: TanStack Query Migration (revised — manual refresh deferred, staleTime confirmed 30s)

## Intent

Every client-side navigation refetches. `frontend/src/shared/api/useApiQuery.ts` holds state in `useState`/`useEffect` scoped to the mounting component, so leaving Dashboard for Expenses and coming back re-hits the API; `apiClient.fetch`'s 100ms in-flight dedup Map is not a cache. Meanwhile every mutating child hand-threads a `refresh()`/`onRefresh()` closure to its parent — there is no shared invalidation key space, so "which lists does this write affect" is re-decided at each call site and already drifts.

Adopt `@tanstack/react-query` v5 as the single client cache. Two outcomes this change delivers: (1) navigation serves from cache instead of the network; (2) in this shared multi-user group-expense app another member's edit surfaces promptly via staleness + window-focus refetch. An explicit manual-refresh UI affordance is deferred (D7) — every hook still exposes `refetch()` for a future change to surface. Affected workspace: frontend only.

## Scope

### In Scope
- Add `@tanstack/react-query` to frontend; `createQueryClient()` factory + app singleton in `frontend/src/shared/api/queryClient.ts`; typed key factory in `frontend/src/shared/api/queryKeys.ts`.
- `QueryClientProvider` mounted in `App.tsx` above `AuthProvider` (D4); cache cleared on sign-out (D5).
- Read hooks (`dashboardHooks.ts` x4, `savingsHooks.ts`, `GroupListContext.tsx`) rebacked by `useQuery` behind their current return shape (thin wrappers); `useApiQuery.ts` deleted once its last consumer is migrated. These four files have zero tests today — this change adds them.
- Mutations to `useMutation` + `invalidateQueries`, removing `refresh`/`onRefresh` prop-drilling: `SavingsGoalForm`, `SavingsGoalList`, `InlineAllocationEditor`/`useContributionSession`, `ExpenseForm`, `ExpensesPage`, `TransfersPage`, `useIncomeSession` consumers, `GroupsPage`/`CreateGroupForm`.
- Normalize the two direct `apiClient.fetch` mutation sites into entity API modules: `BudgetCategories.tsx` (category-create/update, transfer-create) and `DashboardPage.tsx` (category-delete) — D3.

### Out of Scope
- Manual refresh affordance (D7) — deferred to a future change (user explicitly said "leave it for now"). Users get cache-served navigation and focus/staleness refetch in this change; an explicit "refresh now" button is not part of this slice. `refetch()`/`invalidateQueries` remain available at the hook level for a later change to surface in the UI.
- Supabase Realtime / push invalidation — explicitly not part of this product slice. Focus + staleness refetch is the agreed freshness mechanism.
- `frontend/src/pages/profile/ui/useProfileForm.ts` and `AuthProvider`'s raw `/api/users/me` fetch (D3): no shared query to invalidate, auth bootstrap must not depend on the cache layer.
- Dead API surface `groupApi.invitations.*`, `groupApi.archive.*`, `groupApi.transferOwnership` (zero UI consumers) — not migrated, not key-designed for.
- `apiClient.fetch` transport itself (stays the queryFn/mutationFn), `ActiveGroupContext`, optimistic updates, offline/persisted cache, prefetching, suspense, API/shared/Prisma.

## Approach

Thin wrapper hooks over `useQuery`, keeping `{ data, loading, error, refresh, isInitialLoading }` at consumer boundaries. Bounds blast radius to the four untested files, keeps `ActiveGroupSync.test.tsx`'s module mock and entity-API-mocking widget tests valid, lets new coverage land inside this change.

## Decisions (D1-D7)

- D1 — KEEP `GroupListProvider` as thin Context over `useQuery` (user-confirmed). Cache sharing comes from TanStack either way; keeping the Context means `ActiveGroupSync.tsx`/`.test.tsx` and `GroupsPage.tsx` are untouched.
- D2 — Global `staleTime: 30_000` (user confirmed 30s after clarifying staleTime is not a polling interval — it only gates refetch-on-focus/mount/reconnect, no background timer), `refetchOnWindowFocus: true`, `refetchOnReconnect: true`, `gcTime: 5min`, `retry: 1`. Override: `["groups"]` -> `staleTime: 5min`.
- D3 — Migrate the two `apiClient.fetch` mutation sites (`BudgetCategories.tsx`, `DashboardPage.tsx` category-delete); leave `useProfileForm`/`AuthProvider` raw fetches alone.
- D4 — `QueryClientProvider` outermost, wrapping `BrowserRouter` > `AuthProvider`. Load-bearing: `AuthProvider` renders `{!loading && children}` so its subtree unmounts on session bootstrap/`retrySessionLoad`; a client below it would lose the cache each revalidation.
- D5 — `queryClient.clear()` when session goes null (sign-out/expiry), not on token refresh. Shared-device privacy requirement (user confirmed) — household co-members share groupIds so key namespacing isn't a substitute. Gate on session-null/user-id change (existing `checkedUserIdRef` pattern), never the raw Supabase event (it re-emits SIGNED_IN on tab focus).
- D6 — Keys: `["groups"]`, `["group", groupId, <resource>, ...filters]`; mutations invalidate the `["group", groupId]` prefix by default.
- D7 — DEFERRED, not built this change (user explicitly deferred). Manual refresh stays available as `refetch()`/`invalidateQueries(["group", groupId])` at the hook level; no UI ships now. Every hook still returns `refetch` for a future change to surface.

## Delivery

3 PR slices (not 4 — slice 4 "refresh affordance" removed since D7 is deferred): (1) dep + client + keys + provider + logout clear; (2) read hooks + their new tests; (3) mutations + invalidation. `useApiQuery.ts` deleted only at the end of slice 2.

Chain strategy: feature-branch-chain (user-confirmed) — each slice PR targets a `tanstack-query-migration` tracking branch; only the tracking branch merges to `develop`, once all slices land and are confirmed working. Delivery strategy: ask-on-risk resolved via this explicit chain choice.

## Risks
Same as before minus the refresh-affordance risk; see full table in `openspec/changes/tanstack-query-migration/proposal.md` (source of truth, kept in sync with this Engram copy).

## File
Full proposal lives at `/home/tomas/projects/calculoides/openspec/changes/tanstack-query-migration/proposal.md` (hybrid artifact store) — read that file for the complete Affected Areas / Risks / Success Criteria / Downstream tables; this Engram copy is a synced summary after the D7-deferral and staleTime-confirmation revision.

observations.title: sdd/tanstack-query-migration/spec
observations.content:
# Client Data Cache Specification

## Purpose
Defines the client-side caching, staleness, and invalidation contract for group-scoped API reads and writes, replacing per-component refetch-on-mount with a shared query cache. Cache clearing on sign-out is a privacy requirement for shared-device use, not merely a UX nicety.

## Non-Goals
- No manual "refresh now" UI control ships in this capability. refetch()/invalidateQueries remain available at the hook level for a future change to surface.
- No Supabase Realtime or other push-based invalidation; staleness + focus refetch is the only freshness mechanism.
- useProfileForm.ts and AuthProvider's raw /api/users/me fetch are not backed by this cache.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Cache-Served Navigation Within Staleness Window
The system MUST serve previously fetched group-scoped data from cache, with no new network request, when a query is remounted within its staleness window (30 seconds by default).
#### Scenario: Return to a page within the staleness window
- GIVEN a user fetched Dashboard data 10 seconds ago
- WHEN the user navigates to Expenses and back to Dashboard
- THEN Dashboard renders instantly from cache and issues no new request

### Requirement: Refetch Only on Remount or Refocus, Never on an Interval
Once a cached query becomes stale, the system MUST refetch it only when it becomes active again — on component remount, on window refocus (refetchOnWindowFocus: true), or on network reconnect (refetchOnReconnect: true). The system MUST NOT poll on a fixed interval; no query MUST configure refetchInterval.
#### Scenario: Stale query refetches on remount
- GIVEN a query's data is older than its staleTime
- WHEN the component consuming it mounts
- THEN a background refetch fires and the view updates when it resolves
#### Scenario: Stale query refetches on window refocus
- GIVEN a backgrounded tab holds stale group data
- WHEN the user refocuses the tab
- THEN a background refetch fires, surfacing another member's edit without a manual reload
#### Scenario: No refetch while the tab stays focused and idle
- GIVEN a query is within its staleness window
- WHEN no remount, refocus, or reconnect occurs
- THEN no automatic request is made

### Requirement: Extended Staleness for the Group List
The ["groups"] query MUST use a 5-minute staleTime, overriding the 30-second default, since group membership changes rarely.
#### Scenario: Group list stays cached across a short session
- GIVEN the group list was fetched 2 minutes ago
- WHEN any component remounts a groups query
- THEN no refetch occurs because the list is still within its 5-minute window

### Requirement: Bounded Retry on Failed Queries
Failed queries MUST retry at most once (retry: 1) before surfacing an error, to avoid retry storms on non-transient failures such as 401 or 404.
#### Scenario: Query fails with 404
- WHEN a group-scoped query fails with a 404
- THEN it retries once, then surfaces an error state without further automatic retries

### Requirement: Full Cache Clear on Sign-Out
The system MUST clear the entire query cache when the session transitions to signed-out (session becomes null), and MUST NOT clear it on a token refresh.
#### Scenario: Shared device — user switch leaves no residual data
- GIVEN User A is signed in on a shared browser tab with cached group, summary, and expense data
- WHEN User A signs out and User B signs in on the same tab
- THEN User B's first render shows no flash of User A's cached data — the cache is cleared before User B's session is established
#### Scenario: Token refresh does not clear the cache
- GIVEN a signed-in user with cached data
- WHEN the session token silently refreshes
- THEN the cache is untouched and no refetch is forced

### Requirement: Mutations Invalidate Group-Scoped Queries by Key Prefix
After any group-scoped mutation (expense, category, transfer, savings goal, or income write) succeeds, the system MUST mark every cached query under the ["group", groupId] key prefix as stale, triggering a refetch for any of those queries currently mounted.
#### Scenario: Expense mutation refreshes dependent views
- GIVEN a group's summary and expense list are both mounted and cached
- WHEN a new expense is created for that group
- THEN both the summary and expense list refetch without either component being told to refresh directly
#### Scenario: Mutation for one group does not affect another
- GIVEN Group X and Group Y both have cached data
- WHEN a mutation succeeds for Group X
- THEN Group Y's cached queries are not marked stale

## File
Filesystem copy: openspec/changes/tanstack-query-migration/specs/client-data-cache/spec.md (hybrid artifact store, source of truth kept in sync).

observations.title: sdd/tanstack-query-migration/design
observations.content:
# Design: TanStack Query Migration

Artifact store: hybrid. Full source of truth: `/home/tomas/projects/calculoides/openspec/changes/tanstack-query-migration/design.md` (read that file for the complete Interfaces/Contracts TypeScript, File Changes and Testing Strategy tables). This Engram copy is a synced summary.

## Technical Approach

TanStack Query v5 becomes the cache; `apiClient.fetch` stays the transport. The six read hooks keep their EXACT current 5-field return shape (`{data, loading, error, refresh, isInitialLoading}`), so every page/widget consumer and every existing `vi.mock`/`mockReturnValue` compiles unchanged — slice 2 touches zero page files. Typed key factory (`queryKeys.ts`) + `createQueryClient()` (`queryClient.ts`) carry D2/D6. Mutations move to `useMutation` + prefix `invalidateQueries`. `AuthProvider` gets the client via `useQueryClient()` (only possible because D4 mounts the provider above it) and clears on owner change.

## Architecture Decisions (A1-A10)

- A1 — Wrapper return type = today's 5 fields + OPTIONAL `isFetching?`/`refetch?`. Evidence: `expenses-page.test.tsx:167` and `groups.test.tsx:30` call `mockReturnValue({...exactly 5 fields})` against the real type; a required 6th field fails typecheck. Optional fields satisfy D7's "every hook still exposes refetch".
- A2 — `isInitialLoading` KEEPS its name and equals `loading`. Renaming to `isPending` touches every consumer + `expenses-page.test.tsx:192` for zero gain.
- A3 — `error` stays `string | null` via shared `toErrorMessage()`. `DashboardPage.tsx:120` renders `{summaryError ?? categoriesError}` directly in JSX; `groups.test.tsx:94` asserts a string. An `Error` in JSX is a runtime break.
- A4 — `loading` <- `isLoading` (= isPending && isFetching), NOT `isFetching`. Prevents full-surface skeleton on every window-focus refetch, and stays `false` for a disabled query (`isPending` alone stays true forever when `enabled: false`, breaking the `groupId === null` case).
- A5 — `data: query.data ?? MODULE_LEVEL_FALLBACK` preserves `DashboardSummary | null` / `CategoryWithBalances[]` signatures. Fallback must be a module constant (fresh `[]` per render breaks referential equality).
- A6 — `AuthProvider` uses `useQueryClient()`, not the module singleton, so a test's own client is the one cleared. Cost: `AuthProvider.test.tsx` must be wrapped in a provider (slice 1).
- A7 — Clear gated on a dedicated `cacheOwnerIdRef` mirroring the `checkedUserIdRef` pattern (not reusing it: that ref means "profile already checked" and is nulled on token-less states). Never fires on mount or token refresh.
- A8 — `placeholderData: keepPreviousData` on the two paginated hooks only; do NOT fold `isPlaceholderData` into `loading` (that re-shows the skeleton and buys nothing). Filters already in the key, so page 1 survives page 2.
- A9 — `GroupListContext.tsx` lands in SLICE 2, not slice 1 (resolves the proposal's unassigned file). Slice 1 stays a zero-behaviour-change infra PR; its D5 test seeds the cache with `client.setQueryData` instead of depending on a migrated hook.
- A10 — New entity modules must reproduce the EXACT endpoint strings and JSON bodies, because `BudgetCategories.test.tsx` mocks `apiClient.fetch` and asserts the payload; then slice 3 only adds a provider wrapper and drops the `onRefresh` assertions.

## Key contracts

- Keys: `queryKeys.groups()`, `.group(g)` (invalidation prefix), `.summary/.categories/.savingsGoals(g)`, `.expenses(g, filters)`, `.transfers(g, filters)`; filters stripped of `undefined` before hashing. `NO_GROUP = "__no-group__"` placeholder for disabled queries.
- `createQueryClient(o)` merges PER SECTION (`queries`/`mutations`), not by top-level spread, so test overrides don't drop D2 defaults. Exports `BASE_QUERY_DEFAULTS` for assertion; `setQueryDefaults(["groups"], {staleTime: 5min})`.
- `toApiQueryResult(q, fallback)` is the single mapping point for A1-A5.
- Mutation rule: RETURN the `invalidateQueries` promise from `onSuccess` when success closes a dialog (v5 awaits it, so the dialog closes on fresh data); fire-and-forget for inline deletes. `mutationFn` gets no `signal`.
- AbortSignal adapter: `queryFn: ({signal}) => api.list(groupId, signal)`; entity fetchers without a signal param gain an additive trailing `signal?: AbortSignal` (matches the `groupApi.list(signal?)` precedent).
- Test client: `createTestQueryClient()` = `retry:false`, `gcTime:Infinity`, `refetchOnWindowFocus/Reconnect:false`, `staleTime:0`, fresh per test.

## Slices + review budget

1. dep + queryKeys + queryClient + toErrorMessage + App.tsx provider + AuthProvider clear + test utils + AuthProvider.test.tsx wrapper. ~200 lines, Low.
2. apiQueryResult + dashboardHooks + savingsHooks + GroupListContext + 3 new test files; delete `useApiQuery.ts` at the end. ~400+, Medium/High — split 2a (dashboardHooks) / 2b (savingsHooks + GroupListContext + deletion) if the forecast exceeds 400.
3. entities/category + transfer.create + BudgetCategories + pages + features mutations. ~600+, High — split 3a (dashboard/category/transfer incl. D3 entity modules) / 3b (savings/expense/group).

## Open questions

- v5 API shapes (`isLoading = isPending && isFetching`, `keepPreviousData` export, `setQueryDefaults`, `onSuccess` promise-awaiting) are from knowledge, NOT fetched docs — the Context7 MCP tool was not exposed to the design executor. Slice 1 must verify against the installed `.d.ts` before slice 2 depends on them.
- Whether `isFetching`/`refetch` get promoted from optional to required in the D7 follow-up.
- Whether paginated pages surface `isFetching` now or with D7.

## Threat matrix

N/A — no routing/shell/subprocess/VCS-automation/executable-classification boundary. The one security-relevant requirement is D5 (cross-user cache leak on a shared device), covered by three RED tests in `AuthProvider.test.tsx`.

### Final holistic check: `apiClient`'s in-flight dedup Map (`frontend/src/shared/api/client.ts`)

Still worth keeping, unchanged. It dedupes identical `method:endpoint:body` calls within a 100ms window — this is transport-layer protection against **duplicate concurrent calls to the exact same request**, which is a different concern from TanStack Query's cache:
- TanStack Query dedupes concurrent **queries** by query key at the hook layer (above the fetcher), so for `useQuery`-backed reads this Map's dedup role is now largely redundant.
- TanStack Query does **NOT** dedupe **mutations** — `useMutation` never coalesces concurrent calls with the same `mutationFn`/args. It is not made obsolete by this migration — it protects a distinct, still-real failure mode (duplicate in-flight requests) that `QueryClient`'s query-key cache does not cover for mutations or unwrapped calls.
