observations.content:
## Verification Report — tanstack-query-migration

**Verdict: PASS WITH WARNINGS**

### Scope verified
Branch `tanstack-query-migration-05-remaining-mutations`, 5 commits on top of `develop`
(caf4989, fa14e7f, 5dfa56d, 0a00d3f, ed10889). All 48/48 tasks in tasks.md checked off
(`rg -c '^- \[x\]'` = 48, `'^- \[ \]'` = 0).

### Runtime evidence (executed directly, not trusted from apply-progress)
- `npm run test -w frontend -- --run` → 65 files / 424 tests passed. Matches apply-progress claim exactly.
- `cd frontend && npm run typecheck` → clean.
- `npx turbo run typecheck` (root, 3 packages: api/frontend/shared) → 3/3 pass (cache hit).
- `npx eslint .` (frontend) → 0 errors, 7 warnings (react-refresh/only-export-components, pre-existing baseline, none new).

### Spec compliance (client-data-cache/spec.md, 6 requirements / 13 scenarios) — all verified against real code + tests, not just planned
1. Cache-Served Navigation Within Staleness Window — `queryClient.ts` BASE_QUERY_DEFAULTS.staleTime=30_000; `dashboardHooks.test.ts` has real "serves cache on remount within the staleness window (no second fetch)" tests using a client with real (non-zero) staleTime for all 4 hooks (useDashboardSummary/useCategoriesList/useExpensesList/useTransfersList) — genuine cache-hit assertions, not `retry:false/staleTime:0` test-client stubs. PASS.
2. Refetch only on remount/refocus/reconnect, never interval — config has `refetchOnWindowFocus: true`, `refetchOnReconnect: true`, no `refetchInterval` anywhere in `src` (grep confirmed, only reference is a `.toBeUndefined()` assertion in queryClient.test.ts). PASS (config-level, appropriate for a declarative TanStack default; no fake-timer integration test of the retry/refocus mechanics itself — SUGGESTION, not a gap).
3. Extended staleness for `["groups"]` — `GROUPS_STALE_TIME = 5*60_000` via `client.setQueryDefaults(queryKeys.groups(), …)`; unit-tested in queryClient.test.ts. PASS.
4. Bounded retry (`retry: 1`) — present in BASE_QUERY_DEFAULTS, unit-tested. PASS (config-level only, same caveat as #2).
5. Full cache clear on sign-out, not on token refresh — `AuthProvider.tsx` cacheOwnerIdRef gating verified by direct code read: `undefined` baseline on first observation, `queryClient.clear()` only fires when owner id actually changes; three dedicated D5 tests in AuthProvider.test.tsx ("clears... shared-device scenario", "does not clear... token refresh", "does not clear... SIGNED_IN re-emit for same user") using `client.setQueryData` seeding. PASS — matches design A6/A7 exactly.
6. Mutations invalidate by `["group", groupId]` prefix — grepped all 13 `invalidateQueries` call sites in `src`; all group-scoped mutations use `queryKeys.group(groupId)`, the one group-creation mutation (`CreateGroupForm.tsx`) correctly uses the top-level `queryKeys.groups()` instead. Cross-group isolation is structural (different groupId = different key prefix, not asserted by an explicit "Group Y unaffected" test — SUGGESTION for future coverage, not blocking since it follows directly from TanStack's key-matching semantics).

### Proposal Success Criteria — verified against code, not the apply narrative
- Cache-served navigation: verified (see #1 above) — dashboardHooks.test.ts genuinely exercises cache-hit, not staleTime:0.
- Refocus refetch shows another member's edit: declarative via `refetchOnWindowFocus: true`; no integration test simulating a visibilitychange + refetch end-to-end (relies on TanStack's own behavior). Not flagged as CRITICAL — this is standard practice for adopting a well-tested library default.
- No `refresh`/`onRefresh` closure passed to a mutating child: repo-wide grep (my own, not reused from any apply agent) confirms zero `onRefresh` matches in `src`; all remaining `refresh`/`refresh:` matches are exclusively `ApiQueryResult.refresh()` retry-button usage in DashboardPage/SavingsPage/GroupsPage error states (D7) plus GroupListContext's own hook field. PASS.
- Sign-out → sign-in as different user renders no stale data: verified via AuthProvider.tsx code + 3 dedicated tests (see #5). PASS.
- `useApiQuery.ts` deleted, zero references: file confirmed deleted from filesystem; only "reference" repo-wide is a doc-comment in `apiQueryResult.ts` describing the preserved contract by name, not an import. PASS.
- Previously-untested files now covered: `dashboardHooks.test.ts` (493 new lines), `savingsHooks.test.ts` (132 lines), `GroupListContext.test.tsx` (133 lines), `apiQueryResult.test.ts` (88 lines) all confirmed new (`git show 1dbc6db -- <file>` returns empty for pre-migration state) and substantive. PASS.
- `npm test`/`lint`/`typecheck` pass, `ActiveGroupSync.test.tsx` + entity-mocking widget tests pass unchanged: confirmed via full suite run (424/424) and diff review — the only widget test with real assertion changes is `BudgetCategories.test.tsx` (drops `onRefresh` prop/assertions, adds `QueryWrapper` + invalidation spies, exactly the documented exception). All other test-file diffs are either brand-new coverage files or wrapper-only (`QueryWrapper`/`groupId` prop addition, zero behavioral assertion changes) — confirmed by reading the diffs for `tests/pages/expenses.test.tsx` and `tests/widgets/categories.test.tsx`, which were not explicitly named in tasks.md's "documented exception" list but are structurally the same wrapper-only pattern (low risk, correctly unflagged).

### Non-goals — confirmed nothing crept in
- No manual refresh UI added (D7 deferred, confirmed — only retry-button `refresh()` usage exists).
- No Supabase Realtime/channel usage anywhere in `src` (grepped).
- `useProfileForm.ts` untouched (`git diff 1dbc6db..HEAD` empty for that file).
- `AuthProvider`'s raw `/api/users/me` fetch preserved outside the query cache (still a plain `fetch`, not a `useQuery`).
- Dead API surface (`groupApi.invitations.*`, `.archive.*`, `.transferOwnership`) left in place, unmigrated, as specified.

### Diff shape sanity check
`git diff --stat 1dbc6db..HEAD` → 60 files changed, 3166 insertions(+), 592 deletions(-) = 3758 changed lines total (3731 excluding the 27-line lockfile bump). This is ~2x the tasks.md forecast of ~1900. Per-PR breakdown (numstat): PR1=1047 (forecast ~200 — actual overage driven by bundling openspec proposal.md/design.md/spec.md/tasks.md docs, 484 lines, directly into the PR1 commit, not by code bloat), PR2=721 (~420 forecast), PR3=386 (~380, matches), PR4=648 (~480, modest overage), PR5=1034 (~420 forecast — actual overage driven by the wrapper-only `QueryWrapper` fixes rippling into more pre-existing test files than originally scoped, e.g. `memberColorIndex.test.tsx`, `tests/widgets/income.test.tsx`, `expenses.test.tsx`, `categories.test.tsx`). No file outside `frontend/` was touched except the openspec change docs themselves and the root `package-lock.json` (27 lines, expected per proposal's Dependencies section). WARNING: forecast accuracy for the review-workload guard was materially off (~2x), primarily in slices 1 and 5 — worth noting for future SDD sizing calibration, not a spec-compliance defect.

### Issues
- CRITICAL: none.
- WARNING: (1) Total changed-line forecast in tasks.md undercounted actual delivery by ~2x (1900 vs 3758), concentrated in PR1 (openspec docs bundled into the infra PR) and PR5 (wrapper-fix ripple wider than scoped) — a review-workload-guard calibration issue, not a functional defect. (2) `proposal.md`'s own Success Criteria checkboxes are still literally `[ ]` unchecked in the file even though all criteria are verified met by code/tests — cosmetic, should be ticked before archive.
- SUGGESTION: (1) The staleness/refocus/retry-count requirements are verified at the config level (BASE_QUERY_DEFAULTS values + unit tests asserting those values) rather than via an integration test that actually exercises TanStack's refetch-on-focus or retry-then-fail timing; acceptable for a declarative library default but a gap if a future regression silently changes TanStack's own behavior. (2) No explicit test asserting "mutation for Group X does not mark Group Y's queries stale" (Requirement 6's second scenario) — structurally guaranteed by key-prefix design and not contradicted by any test, but not directly asserted either.

### Artifacts referenced
- Engram: `sdd/tanstack-query-migration/spec` (#118), `/tasks` (#120), `/apply-progress` (#121)
- Filesystem: `openspec/changes/tanstack-query-migration/{proposal.md,design.md,tasks.md,specs/client-data-cache/spec.md}`

Decision: migrate calculoides from its current Vite/React SPA + separate Express API (deployed as Vercel functions) to Next.js — adopting real Next features (App Router, Server Components, Server Actions, Route Handlers, middleware-based auth), not a lift-and-shift port. Planned for the near term.

Why: React 19 already, so no component-paradigm rewrite (ruled out Svelte/SvelteKit for this reason — would require rewriting all ~96 components and replacing @base-ui/react with Bits UI, no direct port). Next collapses the frontend + api workspaces into one app, removes the client-side fetch+bearer-token hop for reads (frontend/src/shared/api/client.ts's manual dedup layer becomes redundant with Server Components + Next's request memoization), and likely makes the api/_src dispatcher's ?action= query-param consolidation pattern unnecessary (that pattern looks like a workaround for old Vercel per-function limits, worth re-verifying against current limits before porting it as-is).

How to apply: when scoping new frontend/api work before the migration lands, avoid deepening investment in the current dispatcher/action-param pattern or the client-side apiClient dedup logic, since both are slated for removal. Bun migration (separately discussed) was scoped as package-manager/CI only, not a runtime swap — unrelated to this decision but discussed same session.

observations.title: sdd/nextjs-migration/explore
observations.content:
## Exploration: Migrate calculoides from Vite/React SPA + Express-style Vercel API to a single Next.js app

### Current State

**Two Vercel-deployed workspaces sharing one project/deployment:**
- `frontend/` — Vite 8 + React 19 SPA, React Router 7 (`BrowserRouter`), TanStack Query, Tailwind 4, Base UI. Entry: `frontend/src/app/App.tsx` defines all client-side routes (`/login`, `/signup`, `/complete-profile`, `/forgot-password`, `/reset-password`, and a protected `/*` subtree: `dashboard/:groupId`, `groups`, `expenses/:groupId`, `profile`, `transfers/:groupId`, `savings/:groupId`).
- `api/` — plain Vercel serverless functions, NOT a framework. Root-level entry files `api/groups.ts`, `api/users.ts`, `api/transactions.ts`, `api/members.ts` are the actual deployed functions (4 total); each is a 3-line re-export of `api/_src/handlers/{name}.ts`. Every handler is wrapped `withErrorHandling(withAuth(...))` and internally calls `dispatch(req, res, routes, defaultAction)` from `api/_src/utils/dispatcher.ts`, which reads `?action=` (or an HTTP-method default: GET→list, POST→create, PUT/PATCH→update, DELETE→delete) and looks up a handler in a `routes: RouteConfig` map.
- Root `vercel.json` maps friendlier logical paths to `?action=` query strings via `rewrites` (e.g. `/api/expenses` → `/api/transactions?action=expenses`, `/api/archive` → `/api/groups?action=archive`, `/api/members/:id/income` → `/api/members?action=update-income&id=:id`), plus a catch-all `/(.*)` → `/index.html` SPA fallback.
- Local dev uses a hand-rolled Express server (`api/_src/server.ts`) that recursively loads `api/_src/handlers/*.ts`, mounts them, and re-applies the same `vercel.json` rewrites so local behavior matches Vercel's rewrite/dispatch semantics — meaningful duplicated infra that a Next.js migration would delete entirely (App Router route files replace both the rewrite table and the Express shim).

**Action inventory (what must become Route Handlers / Server Actions):**
- `groups` handler routes: `list`, `create`, `archive`, `transfer` (ownership), `invitations`, plus a Zod-parsed body action `respond-invite` (ACCEPT/REJECT). Root vercel.json also implies `undo-archive` on the same handler.
- `transactions` handler routes: `summary` (default), `expenses`, `transfers`, `transaction` (GET single / PUT update / DELETE, branches internally on `req.method`), `savings` (branches into `savings-goals-list` / `savings-goal-create` / `savings-goal-update` / `savings-goal-delete` by method), `savings-contribution` (branches `savings-contribution-upsert` / `-delete`), `categories-list`.
- `users` handler routes: `upsert` (default, POST), `me` (GET).
- `members` handler routes: `list` (default), `update-income`, `remove-member`.

**Auth/authorization (the RLS/authorization fix branch this session is on):**
- Frontend: `frontend/src/shared/api/supabase.ts` creates a browser Supabase client (anon key). `AuthProvider` (`frontend/src/app/providers/AuthProvider.tsx`) bootstraps the session via `supabase.auth.getSession()`, listens to `onAuthStateChange`, and does a manual `fetch('/api/users/me', {Authorization: Bearer <access_token>})` to detect an incomplete profile (404) — this duplicate profile-check network round trip is a Next.js Server Component/Server Action candidate.
- `frontend/src/shared/api/client.ts` (`apiClient.fetch`) is the shared fetch wrapper: reads the current session token from Supabase, attaches `Authorization: Bearer <token>` to every request, dedupes in-flight requests by cache key, and races against an `AbortSignal`. This entire bearer-token hop over `fetch('/api...')` disappears once reads move to Server Components/Server Actions co-located in the same Next.js process — no more client→own-API round trip for data that could be fetched server-side.
- API: `api/_src/services/auth.ts` creates a server-side Supabase client (anon key, `persistSession: false`) and exposes `getUserFromSession(token)` (`supabase.auth.getUser(token)`) and `extractTokenFromHeader`. `api/_src/middleware/handler.ts`'s `withAuth` extracts the Bearer token, validates it per-request, and attaches `user` to the request before calling the handler.
- **Critical finding — RLS is NOT actually enforced on API traffic today.** `api/_src/utils/prisma.ts` connects to Postgres directly via `pg.Pool` + `PrismaPg` adapter using `DATABASE_URL` (a raw connection string, not through Supabase's PostgREST layer), and never sets a `request.jwt.claims`/`auth.uid()` session variable. This means the RLS policies in `prisma/rls.sql` (and the newly-added `prisma/migrations/20260804000001_add_missing_rls_policies/`) protect only paths that query Postgres through Supabase's REST/JS-client layer with the user's own JWT (which the current app does not do for domain data — only for `auth.getUser`/`auth.getSession`). All authorization for API-driven mutations and reads is enforced by **explicit in-handler checks** (e.g. `GroupService.isOwner`, `groupMember.findUnique` membership lookups), which is exactly what the current branch's commits (`ef2221c`, `ae9c3d8`, `109250d`) are patching — e.g. `members.ts`'s `remove-member` route was fixed to derive authorization from the *target member's own* `groupId` (looked up from the DB) rather than trusting a caller-supplied `groupId`, closing a cross-group privilege-escalation hole.
- **Implication for the Next.js migration**: Route Handlers/Server Actions that replace these handlers MUST port the same explicit ownership/membership checks verbatim — RLS is a secondary/defense-in-depth layer for any future direct-Supabase-client data access, not a substitute for app-layer authorization, since Prisma will keep bypassing RLS via direct `DATABASE_URL` connection unless the migration deliberately changes the DB access strategy (out of scope unless explicitly decided).
- Recommended target pattern per current Supabase guidance: adopt `@supabase/ssr` (the `@supabase/auth-helpers-nextjs` package is deprecated) with three clients (browser, server/RSC, middleware), a `middleware.ts` that refreshes the session token on every request, and `supabase.auth.getUser()` (not `getSession()`) for server-side authorization checks in Route Handlers/Server Actions/Server Components, per Supabase's official Next.js App Router guide.

**Vercel function-limit hypothesis — CONFIRMED.** Verified against current Vercel docs (fetched 2026-08-05):
- `vercel.com/docs/limits`: "Functions Created per Deployment" = **Hobby: Framework-dependent, Pro/Enterprise: ∞ (no limit)**.
- `vercel.com/docs/functions/runtimes#functions-created-per-deployment`: "When using Next.js or SvelteKit on Vercel, dynamic code ... will be bundled into the fewest number of Vercel Functions possible ... it's unlikely you'll hit the limit of 12 bundled Vercel Functions per deployment. When using other frameworks, or Vercel Functions directly without a framework, every API maps directly to one Vercel Function ... For Hobby, this approach is limited to 12 Vercel Functions per deployment."
- calculoides' `api/` is exactly this "Vercel Functions directly without a framework" case: 4 top-level files = 4 functions today, comfortably under 12, but the `?action=` dispatcher inside each is precisely the workaround that keeps ~20 logical actions consolidated into 4 physical functions instead of one function per action (which would risk exceeding 12 on Hobby as the API surface grows, e.g. transactions alone has ~10 logical actions). Under Next.js, this consolidation is automatic and framework-managed — the `?action=` dispatcher pattern, the `vercel.json` rewrite table, and the local Express dev-server shim (`api/_src/server.ts`) all become unnecessary and should be deleted, replaced by one Route Handler file (or Server Action) per logical resource action.

### Affected Areas
- `api/*.ts` (groups, users, transactions, members entry points) — become Route Handlers under `app/api/**/route.ts` or, preferably, Server Actions for mutations invoked from Server/Client Components.
- `api/_src/handlers/*.ts`, `api/_src/utils/dispatcher.ts`, `api/_src/middleware/handler.ts`, `api/_src/server.ts` — dispatcher/rewrite/local-dev-shim infra to be deleted; per-action auth/error handling replaced by Next.js middleware + a thin auth helper.
- `api/_src/services/auth.ts`, `frontend/src/shared/api/supabase.ts` — replaced by `@supabase/ssr`-based server/browser/middleware clients.
- `frontend/src/app/App.tsx`, all of `frontend/src/pages/**` — become `app/**/page.tsx` (App Router segments); route-level auth guard (`ProtectedRoute`) becomes `middleware.ts` + per-segment `layout.tsx` checks.
- `frontend/src/app/providers/AuthProvider.tsx`, `AuthContext.ts`, `ProtectedRoute.tsx` — client-side session bootstrap and the `/api/users/me` profile-completeness check likely become server-rendered (Server Component reads user + profile in one pass) instead of a client `useEffect` + fetch.
- `frontend/src/shared/api/client.ts` (`apiClient.fetch`) — the bearer-token fetch wrapper is only needed for client components that still need to trigger mutations that aren't Server Actions (e.g. optimistic UI); most current usages likely collapse into Server Actions or `fetch` from Server Components without the manual token attachment (session cookie handles it via `@supabase/ssr`).
- `vercel.json` — rewrites section deleted; only non-API config (if any) remains, or file removed entirely.
- `package.json` (root) — `workspaces: [frontend, api, shared]` collapses to a single Next.js app + `shared`; `turbo.json` tasks simplify (no more `start:api`/`start:api:local`/`dev:local` split).
- `frontend/playwright.config.ts` — `webServer` command changes from `vite dev`/`preview` to `next dev`/`next start`; base URL logic likely unchanged.
- Test suites: `api/_tests/**` (Vitest, unit + integration, incl. `groups.test.ts`, `expense-update.test.ts`, `date-coercion.test.ts`, `archive.test.ts`, `invitations.test.ts`, `server.test.ts`) need re-homing/rewriting against Route Handlers/Server Actions instead of raw handler functions; `frontend/src/**/*.test.tsx` (Vitest + Testing Library) mostly portable as-is for client components, but anything testing `AuthProvider`/`ProtectedRoute` needs rework for Server Component/middleware auth.
- `prisma/rls.sql`, `prisma/migrations/20260804000001_add_missing_rls_policies/` — RLS policies stay relevant only if the migration also changes how the DB is accessed (currently bypassed by direct Prisma `DATABASE_URL` connection); otherwise these remain a secondary safety net, not the enforcement mechanism, and must not be treated as "the migration already covers authorization."
- `.github/workflows/*` — no workflow currently runs `npm test`/`build`/`typecheck` (only `fallow` audit/dead-code scans exist); a Next.js migration is a good moment to also add a CI gate for tests/build, though that's an adjacent decision, not required by the migration itself.

### Approaches

1. **Full incremental App Router migration (recommended)** — bring `frontend/` and `api/` into one `app/` directory Next.js project; convert each `?action=` route to an explicit Route Handler (`app/api/{resource}/{action}/route.ts`) or, where the action is a mutation triggered from a form/UI event, a Server Action; convert SPA pages to Server Components that fetch data directly (Prisma) at render time, with Client Component islands for interactive pieces (dialogs, forms, the Savings Calculator's live recompute); adopt `@supabase/ssr` + `middleware.ts` for auth.
   - Pros: eliminates the two-workspace split, the dispatcher/rewrite indirection, and most client-side fetch+bearer-token hops for reads (server already has the session via cookies); enables streaming/partial rendering for dashboard-heavy pages; single deploy, single Vercel Functions bundle managed automatically (avoids ever hitting the 12-function Hobby ceiling as the action surface grows).
   - Cons: largest surface area — every one of the ~20 logical actions needs a deliberate Server Action vs. Route Handler decision; every explicit authorization check (recently hardened on this branch) must be manually ported and re-verified, not implicitly inherited; Playwright/Vitest suites need meaningful rework, not just import-path updates; risk of quietly reintroducing an authorization gap during the port unless each ported check gets an equivalent test.
   - Effort: High.

2. **Lift-and-shift (Next.js as a client-only shell over the existing API surface)** — explicitly rejected by the task framing (not a real Next.js adoption) and inconsistent with the "collapse two workspaces" goal from the prior decision; keeping the same `?action=` dispatcher and bearer-token fetch client under Next.js API routes gains almost none of Server Components/Server Actions and would carry over the exact authorization-check duplication this branch is currently fixing, without the payoff. Not recommended; included only as the rejected baseline.
   - Effort: Low, but Pros are minimal (single deploy only) and it does not satisfy the stated goal.

3. **Phased/strangler migration** — keep `api/` as-is short-term, stand up a Next.js app that proxies to it while migrating page-by-page (e.g. start with read-heavy Dashboard as a Server Component that queries Prisma directly, leave mutation-heavy Savings/Transfers on the old API until later), retiring `api/` once all actions are ported.
   - Pros: lower risk per PR, fits the 400-line PR review budget better, allows the auth/RLS fix branch to land and stabilize independently before the migration begins; natural chunking for `sdd-tasks`' chained-PR guidance.
   - Cons: temporary dual-auth-path complexity (old bearer-token API + new cookie-session Next.js auth coexisting) unless the middleware is designed to validate both from day one; longer overall timeline; must be careful the interim state doesn't reintroduce the exact class of authorization bug just fixed (e.g. a Server Action that forgets the group-membership check the Express handler now has).
   - Effort: Medium (per phase), High (cumulative), but spreads reviewer load.

### Recommendation

Approach 3 (phased/strangler) sequenced toward Approach 1's end state: land the current RLS/authorization fix branch first (already near-complete), then start the Next.js migration with the lowest-risk, highest-payoff slice — replacing the Dashboard read path (currently `GroupService`/`BudgetService` calls proxied through `/api/summary`, `/api/groups`) with Server Components querying Prisma directly, while the four existing `api/*.ts` functions keep serving the remaining actions unchanged. Migrate mutation-heavy flows (expenses, transfers, savings, member management) resource-by-resource afterward, porting each explicit authorization check with an accompanying test before deleting its old handler. Delete the `?action=` dispatcher, `vercel.json` API rewrites, and the local Express dev shim only once all four resource handlers are fully ported — do not run a half-migrated dispatcher and half Route-Handlers state longer than one phase.

### Risks
- Authorization regression: the branch this exploration ran on exists specifically because group-membership/ownership checks were missing or spoofable; a rushed port to Server Actions could silently drop one of these checks since RLS does not backstop them (Prisma bypasses RLS via direct connection).
- Dual auth-model window: during a phased migration, the app will temporarily need to accept both the old Bearer-token flow (Supabase JS `getSession()` + manual header) and the new `@supabase/ssr` cookie-session flow; if middleware only validates one, some routes could become unreachable or, worse, unauthenticated.
- Test debt: `api/_tests/**` (Vitest, ~9 files) directly imports/tests the handler functions and the dispatcher; these tests need to be rewritten against Route Handlers/Server Actions, not just re-pointed — until then there is no regression coverage for ported logic.
- No CI test/build gate today (`.github/workflows/fallow.yml` only runs audit/dead-code scans) — a broken build or failing test could merge silently during the migration unless a test/build workflow is added concurrently.
- Scope creep: the unrelated Bun package-manager evaluation (same prior session) must not get conflated into this migration's PRs/tasks — sequence it separately if pursued at all.
- Base UI (`@base-ui/react`) and Tailwind 4 usage in ~96 components should be largely portable to Next.js Client Components, but any component relying on `window`/`localStorage` at module scope (e.g. `ActiveGroupContext`'s `readStoredGroupId`) needs `"use client"` and SSR-safe guards (already has a `typeof window === "undefined"` check, which is good precedent to replicate elsewhere).

### Ready for Proposal
Yes — architecture, action inventory, and the Vercel function-limit hypothesis are all confirmed with primary sources (current on-disk code + current Vercel docs). The orchestrator should tell the user: proceed to `sdd-propose` with the phased/strangler sequencing recommendation, explicitly scoping the RLS-fix branch as a prerequisite merge, and treating explicit authorization-check porting (not RLS) as the migration's core safety constraint.

observations.title: sdd/nextjs-migration/proposal
observations.content:
# Proposal: Next.js App Router Migration

## Intent

`frontend/` (Vite SPA) and `api/` (frameworkless Vercel functions) are two workspaces held together by hand-built infrastructure: a `?action=` dispatcher in each of the 4 API functions, a `vercel.json` rewrite table mapping friendly paths onto those query strings, and an Express shim (`api/_src/server.ts`) re-implementing both so local dev matches production. That dispatcher exists only to keep ~20 logical actions inside Vercel's 12-function Hobby cap (confirmed: the cap applies to frameworkless deployments; Next.js auto-bundles and is exempt in practice). Every read also pays a client -> own-API bearer-token round trip.

Next.js App Router removes all three pieces of infrastructure as a side effect of adopting the framework, and lets reads render server-side against Prisma directly. Affected workspaces: **frontend, api, shared** (root tooling too).

**Hard constraint**: Supabase RLS does NOT protect API traffic today — Prisma connects via `pg.Pool`/`DATABASE_URL`, bypassing PostgREST, so `auth.uid()` is never set. Every authorization decision lives in explicit in-handler ownership/membership checks, the exact class of check hardened in `ef2221c`/`ae9c3d8`/`109250d`. Each check MUST be ported verbatim WITH A TEST before its old handler is deleted. RLS is defense-in-depth, not a backstop.

## Scope

### In Scope
- Single Next.js App Router app replacing `frontend/` + `api/`; `shared/` retained.
- `@supabase/ssr` browser/server/middleware clients + `middleware.ts` session refresh; `getUser()` for all server-side authorization. Replaces the bearer-token hop and `api/_src/services/auth.ts`.
- SPA routes -> `app/**/page.tsx`; `ProtectedRoute` -> middleware + segment layouts; Dashboard read path -> Server Components querying Prisma.
- All ~20 `?action=` routes -> Server Actions (mutations from UI) or Route Handlers, resource by resource, each with its authorization check and test.
- Deletion of `api/_src/utils/dispatcher.ts`, `api/_src/server.ts`, `vercel.json` API rewrites, `api/_tests/**` rehomed.
- CI workflow gating `npm test` / `lint` / `typecheck` (no such gate exists today).

### Out of Scope
- Changing the DB access strategy so RLS becomes load-bearing. Prisma keeps its direct connection; RLS policies stay as-is.
- Domain behavior changes. No feature, calculation, or UX change ships in this migration.
- The Bun package-manager evaluation — separate decision, must not enter these PRs.
- Removing TanStack Query. It stays for client-owned interactive state; only Server-Component-served reads leave it.
- Redesigning components; Base UI + Tailwind 4 components port as Client Components.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities
- `resource-authorization`: the ownership/membership rules every group, member, transaction, and savings operation MUST enforce at the application layer, stated transport-independently so the port is verifiable rather than tribal knowledge.
- `server-session-auth`: cookie-based session establishment, middleware refresh, server-side `getUser()` verification, protected-segment behavior, and sign-out.

### Modified Capabilities
- `client-data-cache`: which reads remain client-cached once Server Components own the Dashboard read path, and how Server Action mutations invalidate them.

## Approach

Phased strangler toward a full App Router end state. The Next.js app and the existing `api/` functions coexist; `api/` is retired only when the last handler is ported.

| Phase | Slice | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Land `fix/supabase-rls-and-api-authorization`; add CI test/build gate | Prerequisite. No migration code. |
| 1 | Next.js shell: app skeleton, `@supabase/ssr` clients, `middleware.ts`, auth pages, protected layout. `api/` untouched and still serving. | Establishes the dual-auth window. |
| 2 | Dashboard read path -> Server Components + Prisma | Proves the read pattern; highest payoff, no mutations. |
| 3-6 | Port mutations resource by resource: groups+members -> transactions/expenses -> transfers -> savings | One resource per PR. Authz check + test lands before the old handler is deleted. |
| 7 | Delete dispatcher, `vercel.json` rewrites, Express shim, `api/` workspace; collapse `turbo.json`/root scripts; repoint Playwright `webServer` | Cleanup only, after phase 6. |

| # | Decision | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | Strangler, not big-bang | ~20 actions x explicit authz checks is not reviewable in one PR at an 800-line budget; each phase independently revertible. |
| D2 | Both auth paths valid during phases 1-6 | `@supabase/ssr` cookie session for Next.js; existing `Authorization: Bearer` for un-ported `api/` calls. Both derive from the same Supabase session, so `apiClient.fetch` keeps working unchanged. Middleware MUST NOT block `/api/*` legacy paths. |
| D3 | Mutations -> Server Actions; only genuinely external/webhook-ish surfaces -> Route Handlers | Server Actions remove the fetch wrapper and give type-safe args; Route Handlers reintroduce the hand-written request parsing the dispatcher already made expensive. |
| D4 | Prisma stays on the direct `DATABASE_URL` connection | Switching to RLS-enforced access is a separate, higher-risk change. Conflating them means authorization moves layers mid-port. |
| D5 | Authz parity is a per-PR gate, not a final audit | A ported Server Action without its membership/ownership test does not merge. Prevents re-opening the hole `ae9c3d8` closed. |
| D6 | Keep TanStack Query | Ripping it out mid-migration doubles the diff and it just landed. Reads served by Server Components simply stop having a query key. |

## Affected Areas

| Area | Impact | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `app/**` | New | Route segments, layouts, Server Actions, Route Handlers, `middleware.ts` |
| `api/*.ts`, `api/_src/handlers/**` | Removed | Ported resource by resource (phases 3-6) |
| `api/_src/utils/dispatcher.ts`, `api/_src/server.ts`, `api/_src/middleware/handler.ts` | Removed | Framework replaces dispatcher, dev shim, per-handler auth wrapper |
| `api/_src/services/**` (domain services) | Modified | Business logic retained, re-called from Server Actions |
| `api/_src/services/auth.ts`, `frontend/src/shared/api/supabase.ts` | Removed | Replaced by `@supabase/ssr` clients |
| `frontend/src/app/App.tsx`, `providers/AuthProvider.tsx`, `ProtectedRoute.tsx` | Removed | Router + client session bootstrap become App Router + middleware |
| `frontend/src/pages/**`, `widgets/**`, `features/**` | Modified | Move under `app/`; `"use client"` where stateful |
| `frontend/src/shared/api/client.ts` | Modified->Removed | Shrinks as actions port; deleted in phase 7 |
| `vercel.json`, root `package.json`, `turbo.json` | Modified | Rewrites deleted; workspaces collapse to app + `shared` |
| `api/_tests/**`, `frontend/**/*.test.tsx`, `playwright.config.ts` | Modified | Rehomed against Server Actions; `webServer` -> `next dev`/`next start` |
| `.github/workflows/` | New | Test/build/typecheck gate (phase 0) |

## Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| Authorization regression during the port — RLS does not backstop it | High | D5: each ported action ships with its ownership/membership test in the same PR; `resource-authorization` spec is the checklist. Old handler deleted only after its replacement is tested. |
| Phases 2-6 exceed the 800-line review budget | High | Chained PRs on a `nextjs-migration` tracking branch, one resource per PR; split a resource further (read path / mutations) if it still overruns. Only the tracking branch merges to `develop`. |
| Dual auth window leaves routes unauthenticated or unreachable | Med | Middleware matcher explicitly excludes legacy `/api/*`; phase 1 ships an E2E check that both a Next.js page and a legacy API call authenticate for the same session. |
| Test debt: `api/_tests/**` targets handler functions and the dispatcher | Med | Rewrite per resource inside its own phase, never as follow-up. |
| Long-lived half-migrated state | Med | Phase 7 is scheduled, not aspirational; no more than one resource in flight at a time. |
| Client components with module-scope `window`/`localStorage` break SSR | Med | `ActiveGroupContext.readStoredGroupId`'s `typeof window` guard is the precedent to replicate; audited in phase 1. |
| Scope creep (Bun, RLS enforcement, UI redesign) | Med | Explicit non-goals above; reject at PR review. |

## Rollback Plan

Per phase, newest first, on a tracking branch that only merges once complete.
- Phases 0-1: additive. Reverting the shell leaves `frontend/` + `api/` untouched and functional.
- Phase 2: read-only. Revert restores the client-side Dashboard fetches; no data written differently.
- Phases 3-6: each PR deletes one old handler. Revert restores that handler AND its `vercel.json` rewrite together — both must revert as a unit or the friendly path 404s.
- Phase 7: pure deletion; revert restores tooling config. Do not start phase 7 until phases 3-6 are confirmed in production.
- No Prisma schema or migration changes in any phase, so no database rollback is required.

## Dependencies

- `fix/supabase-rls-and-api-authorization` merged (phase 0 prerequisite).
- `next`, `@supabase/ssr` (`@supabase/auth-helpers-nextjs` is deprecated — do not use).
- Vercel project settings switch from frameworkless to Next.js framework preset.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] No `?action=` dispatcher, `vercel.json` API rewrite, or Express dev shim remains.
- [ ] Every authorization check present in `api/_src/handlers/**` at phase 0 has an equivalent check and a passing test against its Server Action or Route Handler.
- [ ] Dashboard renders server-side with no client fetch for its initial data.
- [ ] One deploy, one workspace pair (app + `shared`); `npm run dev` needs no separate API process.
- [ ] CI gates `npm test`, `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` on every PR.
- [ ] Playwright suite passes against `next start`.
- [ ] No user-visible behavior change across the whole migration.

## Proposal question round

Execution mode is `automatic`, so these were not asked interactively. The proposal assumes the bracketed answer; correct any before `sdd-spec`/`sdd-design` start.

1. Timing/urgency — concrete pain (dual-workspace dev friction, approaching the 12-function ceiling) or strategic cleanup? [Assumed: strategic cleanup, no deadline — hence a long phased sequence over a fast big-bang.]
2. Behavior freeze — is "no user-visible change" acceptable for the migration's whole duration, including no new features on pages being ported? [Assumed: yes.]
3. TanStack Query's future — long-term layer, or is eventual removal a goal this migration should aim at? [Assumed: stays; D6.]
4. RLS enforcement — should making RLS load-bearing be a planned follow-up, or is app-layer authorization the permanent design? [Assumed: out of scope here, undecided as a follow-up.]
5. Deployment window — is production running half-migrated (Next.js pages + legacy `api/`) acceptable, or must it land behind one cutover? [Assumed: acceptable; the strangler design depends on it.]

## Downstream (open for spec/design)

- Server Action vs. Route Handler per action for the ~20-action inventory (D3 states the rule; the mapping is a design artifact).
- Where Prisma is instantiated in a Next.js runtime (singleton across hot reloads / serverless invocations).
- Whether `shared/` stays a workspace or folds into the app.
- Exact `middleware.ts` matcher, including legacy `/api/*` exclusion and static-asset skips.
- Error-handling replacement for `withErrorHandling` (Server Action return shapes vs. thrown errors + `error.tsx`).
- Whether phases 3-6 are ordered by risk (groups/members first) or by payoff.

observations.title: sdd/nextjs-migration/spec
observations.content:
# Delta Specs: nextjs-migration

## Domain: resource-authorization (NEW capability — full spec)

### Purpose
Defines the explicit, transport-independent ownership/membership checks every Server Action or Route Handler MUST enforce for group, member, budget (expense/transfer/category/savings), and user resources. These checks are the sole enforcement layer for authorization in this system: they MUST hold whether or not Supabase RLS is also active on the underlying tables, and MUST NOT be weakened, skipped, or delegated to RLS during or after this migration. Ported verbatim from `api/_src/handlers/*`, each check MUST carry a passing test before its source handler is deleted.

### Requirement: Explicit Application-Layer Checks Are Authoritative Regardless of RLS
The system MUST perform an explicit ownership/membership check in the Server Action, Route Handler, or a service function it calls before returning or mutating any group-scoped resource, independent of whatever RLS policy exists on the underlying table.
#### Scenario: RLS active but explicit check absent
- GIVEN a table has an RLS policy that would deny the row
- WHEN a Server Action queries it via Prisma without performing its own membership check
- THEN the request MUST still be treated as unauthorized, because Prisma's direct connection does not evaluate RLS
#### Scenario: RLS inactive or misconfigured
- GIVEN RLS is disabled or misconfigured for a table
- WHEN a request targets a resource the caller does not own or belong to
- THEN the explicit application-layer check MUST still deny it with 403

### Requirement: Group Access Requires Membership or Ownership
The system MUST return a group's detail, member list, or group-scoped data only to a caller who is the group's owner or an existing member.
#### Scenario: Owner reads group — GIVEN owner of group G, WHEN they request G's detail, THEN it is returned
#### Scenario: Non-member denied — GIVEN a non-member/non-owner, WHEN they request G's members or detail, THEN denied 403

### Requirement: Member Income Update Requires Membership
The system MUST allow updating a group member's income only to that group's owner or a fellow member.
#### Scenario: Fellow member updates income succeeds
#### Scenario: Outsider denied

### Requirement: Member Removal Authorization Is Derived From the Target Member's Own Group
The system MUST resolve the authorization group from the target member's own `groupId`, never a caller-supplied one, and allow removal only to that group's owner or self.
#### Scenario: Owner removes a member of their own group — succeeds
#### Scenario: Cross-group id substitution rejected — owner of group A cannot use group A's id to remove a member actually in group B
#### Scenario: Self-removal allowed without ownership

### Requirement: Group-Scoped Budget Resources Require Membership
Reading/writing expenses, transfers, categories, savings goals requires membership/ownership of the resource's OWN group (resolved server-side, not from caller input).
#### Scenario: Member creates expense in their group — succeeds
#### Scenario: Non-member denied on transfer/savings/expense access — 403

### Requirement: Category Deletion Requires Ownership
#### Scenario: Owner deletes category — succeeds
#### Scenario: Member without ownership denied — 403

### Requirement: User Profile Access Is Self-Scoped
`me`/upsert MUST use the session's own user id, never a client-supplied id.
#### Scenario: User reads own profile
#### Scenario: Client-supplied id ignored — system always uses session id

---

## Domain: server-session-auth (NEW capability — full spec)

### Purpose
Cookie-based session establishment, middleware refresh, and server-side verification via `@supabase/ssr`, replacing the bearer-token `Authorization` header flow for Next.js routes. Legacy `api/*` bearer-token routes remain valid in parallel until retired by the phased strangler migration.

### Requirement: Middleware Refreshes the Session on Every Matched Request
`middleware.ts` MUST refresh Supabase session cookies via the `@supabase/ssr` middleware client before any Server Component/Action/Route Handler runs.
#### Scenario: Valid session refreshed transparently on navigation
#### Scenario: Legacy `/api/*` paths excluded from the matcher — middleware MUST NOT intercept them

### Requirement: Protected Segments Require a Verified Session
`getUser()` server-side verification (not mere cookie presence) MUST gate every protected segment/Action/Route Handler touching user/group-scoped data.
#### Scenario: Authenticated user reaches protected content
#### Scenario: Missing/invalid session redirected to sign-in
#### Scenario: Tampered cookie without a valid Supabase session — `getUser()` returns no user, treated as unauthenticated

### Requirement: Sign-Out Clears the Session Server-Side
#### Scenario: Sign-out then request protected content — redirected, no stale cookie accepted

### Requirement: Both Auth Paths Derive From the Same Supabase Session During the Migration Window
Both `@supabase/ssr` cookie session and legacy `Authorization: Bearer` MUST be accepted as long as they derive from the same underlying Supabase session — no double sign-in.
#### Scenario: Same session authenticates both a Next.js page and a legacy API call
#### Scenario: Legacy bearer token from an unrelated/expired session is rejected with 401 independent of Next.js cookie state

---

## Domain: client-data-cache (MODIFIED capability — delta against openspec/changes/tanstack-query-migration/specs/client-data-cache/spec.md)

### ADDED Requirement: TanStack Query Is Retained Only for Client-Owned Reads
Once a read is served by a Server Component, no TanStack Query cache entry MUST exist for it; TanStack Query remains the layer only for Client-Component-fetched reads.
#### Scenario: Server-Component-served read (Dashboard summary) has no query key
#### Scenario: Non-migrated read (e.g. Expenses list) still uses TanStack Query cache exactly as before

### MODIFIED Requirement: Mutations Invalidate Group-Scoped Queries by Key Prefix
(Previously: mutations only needed to invalidate TanStack Query cache entries; no Server-Component data existed to also revalidate.)
After any group-scoped mutation succeeds — via Server Action or client-side API call — the system MUST invalidate TanStack-Query-cached entries under `["group", groupId]` for not-yet-server-rendered resources, AND trigger revalidation of any Server-Component-rendered route serving that group's data.
#### Scenario: Expense mutation refreshes dependent views (unchanged)
#### Scenario: Mutation for one group does not affect another (unchanged)
#### Scenario: Server Action mutation revalidates a Server-Component-rendered route (new) — Dashboard route revalidated + remaining client-cached `["group", G]` queries invalidated

## Notes for sdd-design
- RLS-with-Prisma feasibility (SET LOCAL / session-scoped role) is an OPEN design-owned decision. `resource-authorization` requirements above are written to hold correctly under EITHER outcome — they do not assume RLS becomes load-bearing.
- Full spec files written to `openspec/changes/nextjs-migration/specs/{resource-authorization,server-session-auth,client-data-cache}/spec.md`.

observations.title: sdd/nextjs-migration/design
observations.content:
# Design: Next.js App Router Migration

## Technical Approach

A single Next.js App Router app absorbs `frontend/` and `api/`. The strangler runs *inside* Next from phase 1: a compatibility Route Handler (`app/api/[...legacy]/route.ts`) adapts a `Request` to the existing `ApiRequest`/`ApiResponse` shape and invokes the unchanged exported handlers. This retires `vercel.json` rewrites **and** the Express shim (`api/_src/server.ts`) in phase 1 instead of phase 7, removes the "do root `api/*.ts` functions coexist with the Next preset?" deployment unknown, and gives one place to bridge cookie-session and bearer-token auth. Domain services under `api/_src/services/**` move to `lib/server/services/**` unchanged; Server Actions and Route Handlers call them.

## Architecture Decisions

### Decision: RLS stays non-load-bearing (D4 confirmed — NO-GO)

**Choice**: Prisma keeps the direct `DATABASE_URL` connection. Explicit in-handler / in-action authorization (`resource-authorization`) is the **only** load-bearing layer, in this change and after it. RLS remains SELECT-side defense-in-depth for PostgREST traffic.

**Investigation** (evidence in-repo):

| Finding | Evidence | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| The app connects as the **table owner** | `prisma/rls.sql:170-176`, `prisma/migrations/20260804000001_.../migration.sql:62-68` | Owner bypasses RLS *and* GRANT/REVOKE. Setting `request.jwt.claims` changes nothing — policies are not evaluated at all. |
| Policies are **SELECT-only** (one `UPDATE` on `group_members`) | `prisma/rls.sql` — 11 tables, no INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE policies | Enabling enforcement fails every write immediately. |
| Connection is **PgBouncer transaction mode** | `README.md:20`, `api/CONTEXT.md:3` | Session-scoped `SET` leaks across pooled clients; only `SET LOCAL`/`set_config(..., true)` inside an explicit transaction is safe. |
| Prisma has no per-request session context | Prisma 7.8 — `api/package.json:18` | Every query must be wrapped in an interactive `$transaction` (BEGIN → set_config → query → COMMIT), tripling round trips and pinning a pooled server connection per query. |
| Several checks are not row-visibility rules | `groups.ts:80` owner-only transfer, `transactions.ts:387` owner-only category delete, `members.ts:78` member-derived groupId | RLS turns these 403s into empty results/404 — a user-visible behavior change the migration explicitly freezes. |

**Verdict**: NO-GO. The blocker is not Prisma — the mechanism exists (`FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` on all tables + a non-owner role + `$transaction`-wrapped `set_config('request.jwt.claims', …, true)` via a `$extends` client extension). The blockers are a **database-privilege redesign** and **eleven tables of missing write policies**, both production-outage-risk changes with no relation to routing. A future standalone change may adopt exactly that mechanism; it does not enter these PRs.

**Alternatives rejected**: (a) route domain reads through PostgREST — abandons Prisma, contradicts the constraint; (b) enable enforcement now, keep app checks — writes break; (c) `BYPASSRLS`-off role without FORCE — no effect, owner still bypasses.

**Non-negotiable**: every ported Server Action / Route Handler carries its ownership/membership check and a test in the same PR. RLS never substitutes.

### Decision: Keep TanStack Query; Server Components **prefetch into** it

**Choice**: Server Components fetch first-paint data by calling services directly, then `dehydrate` it into the *existing* query keys behind a `HydrationBoundary`. Client hooks (`useDashboardSummary`, `useCategoriesList`, …) are unchanged.

**Rationale**: App Router sets `staleTimes.dynamic: 0` by default, so client-side navigation back to a Server Component page re-fetches its RSC payload — the exact re-fetch the `client-data-cache` spec forbids ("Cache-Served Navigation Within Staleness Window"). Server Components alone would *regress* that capability. Hydration keeps the 30s/5min staleness contract, focus/reconnect refetch, prefix invalidation, and sign-out clearing intact while removing the client→API waterfall on hard load. Diff for hooks ≈ 0.

**Consequence**: server-prefetched keys still need a GET Route Handler, because a mounted query refetching on focus cannot call a Server Component.

**Alternatives rejected**: (a) drop TanStack Query, push filters to `searchParams` — loses `keepPreviousData` (A8) and cached back-navigation; (b) raise `staleTimes.dynamic` — caches whole RSC payloads, not per-query, and cannot express per-key staleness or prefix invalidation.

### Decision: Server Action vs Route Handler

**Rule**: mutations invoked from UI → **Server Action**. Any read a TanStack query owns (filtered, paginated, or refetch-on-focus) → **Route Handler (GET)**. Reads consumed only at first paint → **direct service call in the Server Component**, no HTTP surface. Server Actions are never query functions: they are POST-only, uncacheable, and serialize per client.

| Surface | Actions |
|---|---|
| Server Component (no endpoint) | `summary`, `categories-list`, groups `list`, `members list`, `savings-goals-list`, `users me` (first paint only) |
| Route Handler GET | `/api/expenses`, `/api/transfers`, `/api/transfers/by-category`, plus refetch endpoints for `/api/summary`, `/api/categories`, `/api/savings` |
| Server Action | group `create`/`archive`/`undo-archive`/`transfer`(ownership), invitations `create`/`respond-invite`, `update-income`, `remove-member`, users `upsert`, expense `create`/`update`/`delete`/`delete-all`, transfer `create`/`delete`/`delete-all`, category `create`/`update`/`delete`, savings goal `create`/`update`/`delete`, contribution `upsert`/`delete` |

### Decision: dual-auth bridged in one adapter

`middleware.ts` refreshes the `@supabase/ssr` cookie session on every non-static request. Its redirect-to-`/login` branch applies **only to non-`/api` paths**; `/api/*` returns 401 JSON instead. The legacy adapter injects a synthetic `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>` from the server Supabase client when the request carries no header, so `withAuth`/`getUserFromSession` still verifies the token. Both paths derive from one Supabase session; `apiClient.fetch` keeps working unchanged.

```ts
// middleware.ts
export const config = {
  matcher: ["/((?!_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico|.*\\.(?:svg|png|jpg|webp)$).*)"],
};
```

## Data Flow

    Hard load:   Browser → middleware (refresh cookie) → RSC page → service → Prisma
                                                            └→ dehydrate → HydrationBoundary → TanStack cache
    Client nav:  Component → useQuery → cache hit (within staleTime) → no request
    Refetch:     useQuery → GET /api/<resource> → Route Handler → authz check → service
    Mutation:    Client form → Server Action → authz check → service → invalidateQueries(prefix)
    Legacy:      apiClient.fetch → app/api/[...legacy] → adapter → withErrorHandling(withAuth(dispatch))

## File Changes

| File | Action | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `app/layout.tsx`, `app/(auth)/**`, `app/(app)/**` | Create | Route segments; `(app)/layout.tsx` hosts AppShell + server-fetched group list |
| `app/(app)/{dashboard,expenses,transfers,savings}/[groupId]/page.tsx` | Create | Server Components; prefetch + `HydrationBoundary` |
| `app/api/[...legacy]/route.ts` | Create → Delete (ph. 7) | Request↔`ApiRequest`/`ApiResponse` adapter + friendly-path→`{handler, action}` table |
| `app/api/{expenses,transfers,summary,categories,savings}/route.ts` | Create | GET endpoints backing TanStack keys |
| `middleware.ts`, `lib/supabase/{client,server,middleware}.ts` | Create | `@supabase/ssr` three-client setup |
| `lib/actions/{group,member,user,expense,transfer,category,savings}.ts` | Create | `"use server"`; shared across pages, not colocated per segment |
| `lib/prisma.ts` | Create | Port of `api/_src/utils/prisma.ts` verbatim (globalThis singleton); server-only import path |
| `lib/server/services/**` | Move | From `api/_src/services/**`, unchanged |
| `vercel.json` | Modify (ph. 1) → Delete | All rewrites removed once the adapter lands |
| `api/_src/{server.ts,utils/dispatcher.ts,middleware/handler.ts}`, `api/*.ts` | Delete (ph. 7) | Framework replaces dev shim, dispatcher, auth wrapper |
| `frontend/src/app/{App.tsx,providers/AuthProvider.tsx,providers/ProtectedRoute.tsx}` | Delete | Router + client bootstrap → App Router + middleware |
| `frontend/src/{shared,entities,features,widgets,pages}/**` | Move | → `components/**`; `"use client"` where stateful |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | Create (ph. 0) | `npm test` / `lint` / `typecheck` gate |

## Interfaces / Contracts

```ts
// lib/actions/result.ts — replaces withErrorHandling for Server Actions.
// Thrown errors are opaque in production builds, so actions return, never throw.
export type ActionResult<T> =
  | { ok: true; data: T }
  | { ok: false; error: string; status: 400 | 403 | 404 | 500 };

// lib/server/errors.ts — one message→status table, reused by both surfaces.
// Ports the existing catch-blocks ("Not a member of this group" → 403, etc.).
export function toStatus(message: string): 400 | 403 | 404 | 500;
```

## Testing Strategy

| Layer | What to Test | Approach |
|---|---|---|
| Unit | Every ported authz check (owner-only transfer/category-delete, member-derived `groupId`, group access on all group-scoped reads) | Vitest against the Server Action / Route Handler, mocking services — one test per check, same PR as the port |
| Unit | `toStatus` mapping, `ActionResult` shapes, legacy adapter (`204 .end()`, `req.query`, bearer injection) | Vitest |
| Integration | Hydration: server-prefetched key is cache-hit on client nav within staleTime; refetch-on-focus hits the Route Handler | RTL + `HydrationBoundary` |
| E2E | Phase 1 gate: one Next.js page **and** one legacy `/api/*` call authenticate from the same session | Playwright against `next dev`/`next start` |

## Threat Matrix

The reference matrix targets shell/VCS/PR process boundaries; none exist here.

| Boundary | Applicability |
|---|---|
| Documentation-like paths | N/A — no file-classification or execution boundary |
| Git repository selection | N/A — no VCS automation |
| Commit state | N/A — no VCS automation |
| Push state | N/A — no VCS automation |
| PR commands | N/A — no PR automation |

HTTP-routing/auth boundary (**applicable**, this change's real adversarial surface):

| Case | Expected safe behavior | RED test |
|---|---|---|
| Unauthenticated request to a protected page | Middleware redirects to `/login` | E2E |
| Unauthenticated request to `/api/*` | 401 JSON, **never** an HTML redirect | Route Handler test |
| Legacy path with a cookie session but no `Authorization` header | Adapter injects the verified token; handler behaves identically | Adapter test |
| Server Action invoked with a `groupId` the caller does not belong to | 403 `ActionResult`, no data touched | Per-action authz test |
| Cross-group id substitution (member of A passes an id from B) | Authorization derived from the resource's own `groupId` (`members.ts:78` precedent) | Per-action authz test |
| Route Handler reached before its authz check ports | Handler does not merge (D5 gate) | CI review gate |

## Migration / Rollout

Phases per the proposal, with two refinements:

- **Phase 1 now also deletes `vercel.json` rewrites and `api/_src/server.ts`**, replaced by the adapter. `npm run dev` needs no second process from phase 1, and rollback is one file, not two out-of-sync ones.
- **Phases 3–6 revert as a single unit** by construction: deleting a handler and removing its entry from the adapter's path table happen in the same file-level change, so a revert cannot leave a friendly path 404ing (the proposal's stated failure mode with `vercel.json`).
- Phase 2 is read-only; revert restores client-side Dashboard fetches (hooks were never modified, only prefetched into).
- No Prisma schema or RLS migration in any phase — no database rollback.
- Phase 7 is pure deletion; do not start until 3–6 are confirmed in production.

## Open Questions

- [ ] Whether `shared/` folds into the app or stays a workspace — decide in phase 1 (leaning: stays; Zod schemas are imported by both server and client code).
- [ ] Phase 3–6 ordering: risk-first (groups/members) is recommended over payoff-first, since groups/members carries the highest authz-regression blast radius.

Retiring/rewriting an E2E test is a bigger call than this task's literal scope ("repoint webServer", "run the suite") — flagged as an explicit open decision rather than silently fixed or silently left broken without mention.

Not applicable in the strict RED→GREEN sense — Phase 7 is pure deletion/config/doc work with no new production logic. **What**: Adopted the `gh stack` CLI extension (`github/gh-stack`, v0.1.0, installed 2026-08-05) for managing stacked PR chains in calculoides, replacing the manual `git checkout -b <branch> && gh pr create --base <previous-branch>` approach.

observations.title: "Save to memory" means Engram, not the file-based auto-memory
observations.content:
**What**: When the user says "save to memory" (or similar phrasing) without further qualification, they mean Engram (mem_save/mem_search/mem_context), not the separate file-based auto-memory system under ~/.claude/projects/-home-tomas-projects-calculoides/memory/.
**Why**: User explicitly clarified this after a prior turn where "save to memory" was interpreted as the file-based auto-memory system instead.
**Where**: Applies to all future sessions in this project (and likely others) — governs which persistence tool to reach for on an explicit save request.
**Learned**: Default to mem_save for any bare "remember this" / "save to memory" instruction going forward; the file-based auto-memory system remains proactive/background bookkeeping, not the target of explicit save requests.
